title: operator-driven IaC hooks for zero-downtime data-plane upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement an operator-driven upgrade orchestration pattern that ties Terraform/IaC outputs and lifecycle hooks to a runtime/data-plane rollout operator so Private (VPC) customers see zero-downtime upgrades and deterministic rollback behavior. The work covers: IaC hooks exposed as module outputs (elb/target group ARNs, internal LB DNS, service-mesh annotations), an operator in the private control plane that consumes those outputs, health-gate evaluation based on latency/error/KV-warm metrics, canary traffic slicing within the VPC (no external DNS changes), and automated rollback triggers tied to circuit-breaker and anomaly detection. This ticket designs the operator hook contract, implements the Terraform module changes, prototypes the operator reconciliation flow, and defines the rollout and rollback playbook for on-call and SRE teams in Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes stable outputs and a lifecycle hook where operator can annotate deployed resources
Operator can perform a shadow deployment of new runtime replicas in the same VPC without touching external DNS
Traffic slicing within the cluster supports 0%, 5%, 25%, 100% transitions controlled by the operator
Health gates include: 95th latency vs baseline, request error rate delta, KV cache hit warmup, and model-serving readiness checks
Automatic rollback triggers on sustained breach (>=2 consecutive 60s windows) and completes with <90s extra downtime in worst-case
End-to-end test harness simulates upgrade with synthetic traffic and asserts zero rejected requests during canary-to-100% transition
Documentation and runbook updated with Terraform example, operator CLI commands, and rollback procedures
rollout_playbook: Step 0: Preflight - run 'tf plan' on private-modules/rt-upgrade and confirm outputs: internal_lb, tg_arn, mesh_annotations
Step 1: Operator bootstrap - operator creates new ReplicaSet with version tag and attaches to internal LB target group in drain-safe mode
Step 2: Shadow warmup - route 0% of production traffic, run KV-cache warmup jobs for new replicas until hit-rate >= 90% of old baseline
Step 3: Canary - shift 5% traffic to new replicas for 10 minutes; monitor KPIs (latency P95, error-rate, tail CPU, model latency distribution)
Step 4: Gradual ramp - 25% for 15 minutes, then 50% for 15 minutes, then 100%; abort and rollback on health-gate breach
Step 5: Cutover validation - confirm telemetry tags, tracing continuity, and SLO dashboards show healthy after 30 minutes
Step 6: Post-upgrade - retire old replicas via operator, emit upgrade-complete event to control plane and mark terraform state as ready
tests: Unit: Terraform module outputs are stable under reapply and changes to subnets
Integration: Operator consumes tf outputs and can reconcile target groups without LB recreation
E2E: Simulated model-heavy workload using loadgen in isolated VPC; assert no request loss across upgrade
Chaos: Kill 30% of old replicas during ramp to validate graceful drain and seamless serving by new replicas
Security: Validate IAM role the operator uses follows least-privilege and KMS access is audited
notes: Design decision: prefer service-mesh traffic-slicing over changing LB weights because many on-prem customers use static internal-load-balancers
Trade-off: implementing dual-stack (old + new) replicasets increases short-term memory footprint but avoids stateful migration during the critical window
Follow-up: implement a post-upgrade KV TTL warmdown to reduce cache-stampedes
Risk: customers with very tight egress/NAT rules may see delayed health telemetry; add a fallback probe via the operator using VPC-internal metrics
